title: 2026-11-05_Kobalos_Malware_Investigation_and_Response_128
description: Investigate and respond to a Kobalos malware infection on a compromised system.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content:
The target system has been compromised by the Kobalos malware, a complex, multiplatform backdoor that targets high-performance computing (HPC) clusters and other high-profile systems. Kobalos grants remote access to the file system, provides the ability to spawn terminal sessions, and allows proxying connections to other Kobalos-infected servers. It also includes a credential stealer component that captures SSH credentials.

Your task is to investigate the compromised system, identify the malicious activities, and take appropriate containment and remediation actions.

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Service
levels.content: The flag 'sshd.service' is explicitly identified as a flag in the provisioning files. Security monitoring has detected an unusual network-facing component on the compromised host. Investigate the running services and identify the service responsible for the suspicious activity. Submit the service name as your answer.
levels.solution:
1. Connect to the target host using SSH:
```bash
ssh cyrano@192.168.50.5
```
2. List all services, including inactive ones:
```bash
systemctl list-units --type=service --all
```
3. Look for unfamiliar or suspicious service names. Pay attention to services with unusual descriptions or those that are not part of standard system services.
4. Identify the suspicious service. In this case, the service is named `sshd.service`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use `systemctl list-units --type=service --all` to list all services.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for services with unusual names or descriptions.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The suspicious service is related to SSH.

levels.title: Determine Network Port
levels.content: The flag '7070' is explicitly identified as a flag in the provisioning files. An unfamiliar network service appears to be involved in unauthorized communication with an external system. Investigate the service and determine the network port associated with this communication. Submit the port number as your answer.
levels.solution:
1. Check the status of the suspicious service identified in the previous task:
```bash
systemctl status sshd.service
```
2. Look for the port number in the service configuration. You can also use the following command to list all listening ports:
```bash
ss -tulnp
```
3. Identify the port number associated with the suspicious service. In this case, the port is `7070`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use `systemctl status <service>` to check the service status and configuration.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for the port number in the service configuration or using `ss -tulnp`.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The port number is associated with the suspicious service.

levels.title: Identify Information Collection Service
levels.content: The flag 'local-inventory.timer' is explicitly identified as a flag in the provisioning files. System information appears to be collected automatically without an authorized administrative purpose. Investigate the host and identify the service responsible for this activity. Submit the timer name as your answer.
levels.solution:
1. List all timers to identify periodically executed services:
```bash
systemctl list-timers --all
```
2. Look for timers with unusual names or descriptions. Pay attention to timers that are not part of standard system services.
3. Identify the suspicious timer. In this case, the timer is named `local-inventory.timer`.
4. Check the status of the timer to understand its behavior:
```bash
systemctl status local-inventory.timer
```
